sources.label: Delaware cyber oversight cases
sources.instrument: Firemen's Retirement System of St. Louis v. Sorenson, C.A. No. 2019-0965-LWW (Del. Ch. 5 Oct. 2021); Construction Industry Laborers Pension Fund v. Bingle, C.A. No. 2021-0940-SG (Del. Ch. 6 Sep. 2022), Final Order and Judgment 13 Oct. 2022, aff'd by order No. 411, 2022 (Del. 17 May 2023); In re The Boeing Co. Derivative Litig., C.A. No. 2019-0907-MTZ (Del. Ch. 7 Sep. 2021); United Food & Commercial Workers Union v. Zuckerberg, 262 A.3d 1034 (Del. 2021); Marchand v. Barnhill, 212 A.3d 805 (Del. 2019); Giuliano v. Grenfell-Gardner, C.A. No. 2021-0452-KSJM (Del. Ch. 2 Sep. 2025); Brewer v. Turner, C.A. No. 2023-1284-KSJM (Del. Ch. 29 Sep. 2025), 2025 WL 2769895, certification denied 2025 WL 3048942 (Del. Ch. 30 Oct. 2025), interlocutory appeal refused sub nom. Turner v. Brewer, No. 444, 2025 (Del. 15 Dec. 2025) (ORDER); In re TransUnion, 324 A.3d 869 (Del. Ch. 2024), C.A. No. 2022-1103-LWW (Del. Ch. 1 Oct. 2024) (Will, V.C.), distinguished in LACERS v. Sanford, C.A. No. 2024-0998-KSJM (Del. Ch. 16 Jan. 2026); Marchner v. Riley, C.A. No. 2025-0164-LWW (Del. Ch. 30 Mar. 2026) (Will, V.C.)
sources.version: dates corrected 2026-08-08; two were wrong before this check. TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS, NEITHER OF WHICH OPENED A SLIP OPINION: the RW-001 dossier's primary-source pass (Chancery PDF headers, the Supreme Court's affirming order quoting its own record) and corroboration from authoritative secondary reporting (Potter Anderson, Morris James), plus the Court of Chancery's published opinion records and CourtListener. This row does NOT claim a slip-opinion read. NO CITATOR WAS RUN - no Shepard's, no KeyCite - so subsequent history beyond the recorded Bingle affirmance is unconfirmed. The Bingle affirmance is an ORDER on the Chancery court's reasoning, not a signed opinion, and the receipt says so (BL-142). READING PASS 2026-08-10 (BL-230): the slip opinions for the four 2024-2026 decisions were READ IN FULL from the courts' own servers - Giuliano, Brewer, In re TransUnion and Marchner from the Delaware Courts opinion server, and the Brewer interlocutory disposition from the Supreme Court's own order. Case numbers, judges, dates and dispositions are taken from those documents. THE BREWER INTERLOCUTORY APPEAL NOW CORROBORATES: Turner v. Brewer, No. 444, 2025 (Del. 15 Dec. 2025), 'IT IS ORDERED that the interlocutory appeal is REFUSED' - parties reverse on appeal, and it is an ORDER not a signed opinion. What was dismissed in Brewer was Count II, the officers, entirely, and Count I as to directors not on the board during the wrongdoing, while the Massey claim was declined rather than rejected; the red flag was a draft complaint sent TO THE BOARD by the former general counsel. CORRECTION OF A CORRECTION, 2026-08-10 (BL-233): an earlier pass recorded here that Brewer contains NO information-systems analysis and that the phrase appears zero times. THAT IS FALSE and it is withdrawn. The plaintiff pleaded both theories; the court addressed the information-systems theory 'in short order' and held there was 'no straight-faced argument that Regions lacked an information system', footnoting Risk Committee, joint Risk-and-Audit Committee and December 2019 / September 2020 BOARD meeting minutes from the 220 production. The zero-count came from searching the extracted PDF text for literal strings the extractor had broken up - it renders the phrase as 'i nformation - s ystems' - so the search proved something about the extraction, not about the opinion. Squeezed-string counts on the same file give informationsystems 3, prongone 1, prongtwo 2. Consequence: the receipts' corollary that the SAME 220 production both disposes of prong one and supplies prong-two knowledge is CORRECT and is restored. Prong one fell away as not seriously contestable, NOT on a merits finding that the system was adequate. In re TransUnion cites Sorenson six times approvingly and Bingle ONCE for black-letter - do not describe it as endorsing Bingle. Marchner gained C.A. No. 2025-0164-LWW and Will, V.C.; its slip opinion's own date line reads 'March 30, 2025' against a 'Date Submitted: December 22, 2025' in the same header, which is a typo in the court's document - the year is 2026. SUBSEQUENT-CITATION SWEEP 2026-08-10 (BL-230), AND IT IS NOT A CITATOR. No Shepard's and no KeyCite have ever been run on this block. What was run is a sweep of a FREE index (CourtListener, Del. Supr. and Del. Ch.) plus a direct read of the one later decision it surfaced. Weaker than a citator in two ways: no editorial treatment flags, and the free index is demonstrably incomplete - it holds NO reporter citation for In re TransUnion while a sitting Chancellor cites that case at 324 A.3d 869. FOUND: no appeal, reversal, vacatur or superseding decision for In re TransUnion, Giuliano, Marchner or Sorenson; the Bingle affirmance date independently confirmed at Del. Supr. No. 411, 2022, filed 17 May 2023; both Brewer WL cites and both dates confirmed by Chancellor McCormick citing her own decisions in LACERS v. Sanford (Del. Ch. 16 Jan. 2026); and In re TransUnion DISTINGUISHED in that same decision on 'effective inaction', pincited 888-90 - its holding stands but the boundary is drawn. The pre-2024 landmarks were NOT swept
sources.intervalBecause: Half the house default, because this block moves and the rest of the repo's gated rows do not. Three of its nine decisions are LIVE litigation - Brewer is interlocutory with the case continuing after the appeal was refused, Giuliano's motion was largely denied so it proceeds, and Marchner is three months old. The 2026-08-10 sweep proved the rate empirically: LACERS v. Sanford distinguished In re TransUnion on 16 Jan. 2026, roughly three months after the previous check, and a 365-day interval would have let that boundary sit unnoticed on a block that goes in front of boards. 180 days is two sweeps a year, which matches the observed movement. It is NOT a substitute for the one paid citator pass, which is separately authorised and still outstanding.

sources.label: DORA ICT risk-management RTS
sources.instrument: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 of 13 March 2024 — Art. 3, point (d)(iii)-(iv); Art. 8(2)(b)(i) (backup and restore requirements of ICT systems, in the ICT operations policy); Art. 25 'Testing of the ICT business continuity plans', incl. Art. 25(2)(c)
sources.version: OJ 25.6.2024; in force 15 Jul. 2024. Arts. 8 and 25 read 2026-08-11 from the EUR-Lex HTML for metric-archetypes.md archetype #7. ⚠️ WHAT ART. 25 DOES NOT SAY, recorded because the page turns on it: there is NO provision isolating periodic backup-restore testing. Art. 25 is a BUSINESS-CONTINUITY testing duty whose scope must COVER backups — 25(2)(c) requires the testing to contain 'the testing of switchover from primary ICT infrastructure to the redundant capacity, backups and redundant facilities'. It sets no drill cadence. Any quarterly-restore-drill figure in CAC is CAC's recommendation and is labelled as such on the page.

sources.label: SEC cybersecurity disclosure rule
sources.intervalBecause: A disclosure clock, where the harm from a missed amendment is a LATE FILING and is asymmetric — nobody is penalised for reading the rule too often. The operative text of these instruments is comparatively stable; the staff interpretation around them is not, and it is the interpretation that moves a deadline. 365 days would let a changed clock sit unnoticed for up to a year on the one artifact whose value is being on time. Halved to 180 on 2026-08-09.

sources.label: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
sources.instrument: NIST CSWP 29 — The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0, Sec. 3.2 (Tiers)
sources.version: CSF 2.0, 26 Feb. 2024. ⚠️ PROVENANCE OF THE Sec. 3.2 READING, stated because it is NOT a fresh read of NIST's paper: the Sec. 3.2 proposition used by metric-archetypes.md archetype #6 was verified on 2026-08-11 against THIS REPO'S OWN vendored Core — skills/nist-csf/references/nist-csf-2.0-core.json, key tiers.guardrail — which quotes CSWP 29 Sec. 3.2 and carries the NIST CPRT export csf-2.0.xlsx at sha256 cc4ec545881141711dacf056e4c806057325b441081f704d9aa32c4eeaf9b616. That is a second-hand read of a first-party artifact, and the distinction matters: if the vendored Core were ever wrong about Sec. 3.2, this row would be wrong with it. The propositions relied on are that Tiers COMPLEMENT rather than replace a risk management methodology, and that progression to higher Tiers is encouraged only when risks or mandates are greater or a cost-benefit analysis indicates a feasible and cost-effective reduction of negative risk. NOTE THE CROSS-CHECK: nist-csf already enforces the same reading as a shipped guardrail (Tiers 'must never be rendered, averaged, or trended' as a maturity score), so archetype #6 and the nist-csf skill now say the same thing, and a change to one should be checked against the other.

sources.label: FBI IC3 Internet Crime Report
sources.publisher: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internet Crime Complaint Center
sources.instrument: 2025 Internet Crime Report — BEC $3,046,598,558 across 24,768 complaints, second-costliest category behind investment fraud; 2025 totals 1,008,597 complaints and $20.877bn
sources.version: 2025 edition. WHAT THIS SOURCE COUNTS, because the number is quoted to boards and the limit travels with it: IC3 reports REPORTED losses from complaints filed with IC3. It is not total economic loss and not an estimate of one - under-reporting is unmeasured, so the figure is a floor of a subset. ALSO: 'wire fraud' is NOT an IC3 category and BEC is. An earlier draft of the sentence this supports said 'BEC and wire fraud'; the report supports only the first, and wire fraud is a federal criminal offence (18 U.S.C. s 1343) rather than a line in this publication. The sentence is pinned to BEC and carries the year.
